bibliography.note: DeMott W. R., Edington J. R. & Tessier A. J. 2004. Limnol. Oceanogr. 49(4, part 2): 1408–1416, as cited.

claims.claim: small Michigan lakes showed "strong energy limitation and weak and sporadic P limitation" of Daphnia
claims.location: p. 1408 (PDF p. 1), Abstract; p. 1409 (PDF p. 2), Methods and Table 1; PDF pp. 5 and 7, Results and Discussion
claims.quote: indicate strong energy limitation and weak and sporadic P limitation
claims.conditions: four small, thermally stratified lakes near Kellogg Biological Station, Michigan (Lawrence, Warner, Little Mill, Baker: 4.8–23.8 ha, maximum depth 7.5–14.0 m, spring TP 8.5–25.1 µg/L), each studied for 5 days in June–July 2001; growth assays of juvenile D. pulex × pulicaria on < 62-µm seston from four depth strata, with phosphate or Synechococcus supplements; centrarchids the dominant fish; large Daphnia (D. dentifera, D. pulicaria) dominated the zooplankton of all four lakes
claims.note: The quote is the abstract's, and the full text bears it out ("effects of P supplements on Daphnia growth were weak and sporadic"; food limitation "largely a consequence of energy limitation"). The paper can drop 'abstract only'. Context the paper's use should carry: these were deep, stratified lakes with abundant Daphnia, and the strong food limitation was tied to Daphnia's own grazing (biomass > 100 µg/L, grazing > 20 % per day), independent of trophic state — not the shallow, Daphnia-poor setting of the analogs.

notes: The paper's sentence calls it 'abstract only'; the full text is now read. Growth improved with depth and was highest on resources from a deep sulfur-bacteria layer partly protected from grazing by low oxygen. Epilimnion 23–25 °C in all four lakes.
